conservative.read: This conservative approach aims for capital preservation with lower volatility. Target returns are modest, around 1.5% per month, with a focus on reducing overall risk and maintaining a cash buffer.

plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to manage concentration.
Reduce leveraged ETFs SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 1%.
Trim leveraged AI/Software (METU) and Semis (MUU) positions.
Increase QQQ to 15% for broader tech exposure.
Initiate a new position in VRT at 4% from the scanner.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth opportunities.
balanced.read: This balanced plan seeks risk-first growth, targeting around 2.5% per month. It reduces leverage and concentration while adding a promising new name and increasing broad index exposure. Expect moderate volatility.

plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to manage concentration.
Increase leveraged ETFs SOXL and SPAL to 6% each.
Increase leveraged AI/Software (METU) and Semis (MUU) to 6% each.
Increase QQQ to 15% for broad tech exposure.

aggressive.read: This aggressive growth plan targets around 4% per month by increasing concentration and leverage, including in leveraged ETFs. Expect higher potential returns but also significantly higher drawdowns and the risk of rapid losses due to leverage and ETF decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Increase QQQI to 30% for enhanced income focus.
Exit all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU) to zero.
Sell high-beta growth names CRWD and SNOW.
Add SPY to 20% for broad market exposure and potential income.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions.
Expect low volatility and reliable income generation.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% per month by prioritizing income-generating ETFs and broad market exposure. Leverage and high-beta single names are cut to near zero. While distributions are prioritized, NAV can still decline in market downturns.
